purpose: Concepts project/paper.txt uses without defining, because it is written for an IR-specialist audience. Flagging these guards against the curse of knowledge when writing for adjacent ML researchers (who are not IR specialists).
assumed_by_source_but_not_by_target_audi: pooling (how candidate documents for annotation are chosen in IR test-collection construction)
in-batch negatives / hard negatives (contrastive-training vocabulary specific to retrieval)
ANN (approximate nearest neighbor) index and its role at retrieval time
nDCG@k, MRR, MAP, Recall@k as IR evaluation metrics and why they differ
the lexical gap (why bag-of-words matching misses semantically relevant documents)
document expansion (docT5query-style) as a retrieval technique
late interaction (ColBERT-style scoring) as distinct from single-vector dense retrieval
TREC-style shared-task conventions (e.g. what a 'track' or 'ad-hoc search challenge' is)
domain shift / task shift as used specifically for retrieval corpora and query types
why MS MARCO is a de-facto standard retrieval training set
assumed_by_target_audience_and_not_redef: supervised fine-tuning of pretrained Transformer encoders (BERT-family)
zero-shot evaluation as a general ML concept (applying a trained model without further training on the target distribution)
basic contrastive/ranking loss intuition (adjacent researchers know this from other subfields, e.g. representation learning)
general notion of a benchmark suite aggregating multiple tasks/datasets
resulting_action: Every term in 'assumed_by_source_but_not_by_target_audience' must be defined at first use in the paper for audience mode B, or replaced with a plain-language description; see story/term_ledger.json.
